second_order: playing with Dash Energy as an April Fool
theme_note: Participants make jokes, laugh, imagine absurd variants, and say they would try the drink; what varies is whether they answer with delight, parody, or continued make-believe.

second_order: working out whether Dash Energy is real
theme_note: Participants challenge the reveal, point to the aprilfools campaign tag, and play with continued uncertainty; the common practice is testing the status of the advertised drink.

second_order: arguing whether the Dash joke was worth the effort
theme_note: Participants judge the joke and its advertising, comparing it with DR1 and answering criticism with a defense of having fun; evaluations vary from trolling and wasted effort to harmless fun.

second_order: asking for useful Dash chargers instead
theme_note: Participants redirect the product tease toward power banks and car chargers, while one reply questions whether a Dash power bank would be efficient; wishes and practical correction vary within the same redirection.
A moderator treats a further Dash Energy link as recently submitted rather than joining the joke discussion; this single code belongs with no other slice-01 practice.

second_order: circulating and spotting Dash-branded April Fools
theme_note: Participants post yogurt translations, energy-drink and soda sightings, and a London event, then wish they had known about a nearby appearance; what varies is whether they circulate a product image, a media sighting, or an event.

second_order: showing, saving, and locating the OnePlus logo
theme_note: Participants show the logo, preserve a screenshot against vandalism, ask where it is, and answer with coordinates; these different turns make the shared mark visible and findable.

second_order: making r/oneplus bigger and fixing its pixels
theme_note: Participants call for a larger mark, volunteer to help, get behind it, and confess and repair a missclick; participation varies from promises to actual pixel repair.

second_order: April fooling oneself with a joyous alternative reality
theme_note: Only the surviving title records this self-directed April Fooling; its deleted body leaves it with no closer practice partner.

second_order: showing a newcomer how to join r/place
theme_note: A newcomer asks how to play, and replies name r/place and explain it as the April Fools toy; question and answers together orient participation rather than locate the existing mark.
Participants report defending the logo, identify nearby growth as pressure, and say the defense is hard; what varies is the work report, the named difficulty, and the assessment of how it is going.

second_order: congratulating the group on the logo
theme_note: This single code celebrates the groups completed work and does not itself enlarge, locate, or defend the mark.

second_order: working out what survived sort of
theme_note: After closure, participants qualify survival, describe the logo as mashed among neighboring marks, react to that description, and ask what the image and event show; the practice ranges from claims and reactions to unanswered requests for explanation.

second_order: making the survival screenshot easier to see
theme_note: Participants complain about the link, recommend a direct Gyazo image, accept and add a mobile link, and debate whether RES solves access; the shared practice is repairing access to the screenshot, with different proposed fixes.
